wiki_text: In July 2024 the Chinese-led CPP-Metron Consortium halted work on the Vasilikos onshore facilities and pier amid a payment dispute with ETYFA; the parties are now in arbitration in London. The FSRU vessel Etyfa Prometheas was delivered in December 2024 but remains idle in Malaysia (reported cost ~EUR 470,000/month to Cypriot taxpayers) because its final commissioning work can only be completed once the Vasilikos pier is finished. Technip Energies has been engaged to assess the works and the government is tendering for a new main contractor (early-stage talks reported with a UAE-based candidate), aiming to select one 'by end of 2026' per Energy Minister Michalis Damianos — no firm terminal-completion date has been given. Total project cost, originally ~EUR 300 million, is now estimated by independent analysis at EUR 1-1.2 billion. Separately, Cyprus is repaying EUR 67 million in EU Connecting Europe Facility grant funds to the European Commission following tender-irregularity findings; both the LNG project and the related GSI electrical interconnector are under European Public Prosecutor's Office investigation for suspected fraud/corruption. Independent analysis (Cyprus Mail, 7 July 2026) suggests realistic first gas is 'towards the end of the decade or around 2030' versus the government's vaguer target of 'well before the end of the decade'.

topic: Why the dead export-terminal record has not been revived
wiki_text: The only post-cancellation revival signal found for the defunct Vasilikos LNG export project is an April 2022 remark by Energean's CEO floating a possible FLNG-at-Vasilikos concept to liquefy the company's Israeli-field gas for EU export; no FEED contract, site agreement, or further public developments have surfaced since. Separately, Cyprus's own offshore gas (the Chevron-operated Aphrodite field and the Eni/TotalEnergies-operated Cronos field, whose development plan the Cyprus cabinet approved in May 2026) is being monetized via a subsea PIPELINE to Egypt's existing LNG processing/export facilities, not via any new Cyprus-sited liquefaction terminal — Cyprus is targeting first offshore gas production by late 2027 on that basis. Taken together, these confirm the Vasilikos export-terminal concept remains dormant with no genuine revival as of mid-2026.
